sentences.text:
This is an appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 arising out of the judgment and award dated 14.08.2018 rendered by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxiliary),
Bhuj (the Tribunal) in Motor Accident Claim Petition No. 815 of 1998 (claim petition), whereby, the Tribunal was pleased to award compensation of Rs.3,29,200/- with running interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization against the claim of Rs.10 lakh with interest and cost made by the appellant - original claimant towards the injuries sustained by him.
Accordingly, the appellant - claimant has preferred this appeal for enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claim Petition No. 815 of 1998
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
2. Facts, briefly stated, are that on 30.05.1998, the appellant - claimant was going from Anjar bus station to the Anjar city walking on the left side of the road, and at around 14:30 hours, when he reached near the traffic point opposite to the Anjar bus station, the C/FA/308/2019 JUDGMENT DATED: 21/06/2023 respondent No. 1, came from behind with a luxury bus bearing registration No. GJ-17-T-1826 in excessive speed and lost control over the bus and dashed with the applicant from behind and the bus ran over the applicant, resulting into applicant's sustaining serious injuries.
3. The petition is filed, inter alia, raising the ground that the appellant - claimant was a Petition Writer and had suffered 45% functional disability for the body as a whole, while he had suffered eight fractures and about eight injuries.

It is submitted by learned advocate Mr. Hemal Shah for the appellant that the appellant had sustained 34% permanent physical disability of the right side limb,
which was assessed by Dr. P. G. Doshi vide Certificate produced at Exh. 54, whereas, Dr. Rajendra B. Trivedi had assessed 22% disability of the head injury.
It is submitted by the learned advocate for the appellant that the claimant - injured was admitted in various hospitals for treatment and had undergone lot of pain and sufferings.

He submitted that the amount under the head of Pain, Shock and Suffering is on the lower side, which is not considered in proportion C/FA/308/2019 JUDGMENT DATED: 21/06/2023 to the injuries sustained and the hospitalization and a long period of treatment.

It is also submitted that during the treatment period, the appellant - claimant was attended by the family members and also an extra attendant was needed; further the appellant - claimant was also required to have special diet because of consistent treatment at various hospitals,
as an indoor as well as outdoor patient.
Further, the appellant - claimant had to expend after transportation, however, the Tribunal has not properly awarded the amount, though evidence was produced on record.

sentences.text: Countering the arguments, learned advocate Mr. H. G. Mazmudar for the respondent - insurance company submitted that the disability which has been assessed, is on the basis as agreed by both the parties.
It is further submitted that the learned Tribunal has erred in applying the multiplier and that has led to grant of excess amount.

It is further submitted that the income has been rightly assessed by the learned Tribunal since the appellant - claimant could not prove his income nor could he lead any evidence to show any possibility of prospective rise in the monthly earnings.

He further C/FA/308/2019 JUDGMENT DATED: 21/06/2023 submitted that the learned Tribunal has granted total medical expenses and in the absence of any evidence, he submitted that the amount granted under various heads is just and proper.
5. As per the appellant - claimant, he was working as a Petition Writer and was earning Rs.4,000-5,000/- per month and was maintaining his family.
Due to the accident, he was admitted and treated in different hospitals by different doctors as an indoor as well as outdoor patient and was operated and has expended towards medical treatment.

He had sustained injuries on his chest,
head, forehead, hands, legs and other parts of the body, resulting into multiple fractures and disability.
The injury had caused loss of income and enjoyment of amenities of life.
He had expended money towards transportation and special diet too.

The learned Tribunal, while appreciating the negligence aspect, had come to the conclusion that the opponent No. 1 came in excessive speed and lost control over the luxury bus and dashed with the claimant who was walking on the road and the front wheel of the bus ran over the claimant and thereby, he sustained serious injuries, which resulted into the C/FA/308/2019 JUDGMENT DATED: 21/06/2023 permanent disability.
5.1 At the time of accident, the learned Tribunal, observing the Discharge Card of Prince Aly Khan Hospital, Mumbai, concluded the age of the appellant - claimant to be 48 years.

A copy of Licence of Petition Writer issued by the Deputy Collector, Anjar - Kachchh was produced on record vide Exh.
107, which was issued on 18.08.1988, just for a period of one year.
It has not come on record by way of any evidence to prove that the said Licence was extended by the Deputy Collector, Anjar - Kachchh for any further period.

The learned Tribunal, thus, having considered the year of accident,
had assessed monthly income of the appellant - claimant to be Rs.3,000/-.
In the absence of any evidence as to the earnings of the appellant, the amount assessed towards monthly income of the appellant - claimant appears to be just and reasonable.
However, the prospective rise in income is required to be considered.

Relying on the decision in National Insurance Company Limited v.
Pranay Sethi & Ors., (2017) 16 SCC 680, and taking into consideration the age of the appellant - claimant, 25% prospective rise in income is C/FA/308/2019 JUDGMENT DATED: 21/06/2023 required to be granted.

sentences.text: Hence, the monthly income of the appellant - claimant would come to Rs.3,750/- (Rs.3,000 + 25%). 5.2 45% functional disability has been considered, as agreed upon by the parties: 34% right side limb and 11% head injury has been assessed.
Taking into consideration 45% disability and the age of the claimant as assessed by the learned Tribunal, the multiplier applicable would be 13.
Considering the annual income, the future loss of income would come to Rs.2,63,250/- (Rs.3,750 x 12 x 13 x 45%).

sentences.text: The learned Tribunal has granted Rs.25,000/- towards Pain, Shock and Suffering, which is required to be enhanced since the appellant - claimant had suffered injuries and over and above the physical injuries, he had suffered head injuries too and was admitted in Prince Aly Khan Hospital at Mumbai and as per the claimant, he had taken treatments, as observed by the learned Tribunal, at various hospitals.

entities.text: Prince Aly Khan Hospital at Mumbai
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Thus, taking into consideration the physical disability as well as the head injury and the treatments taken by the appellant - C/FA/308/2019 JUDGMENT DATED: 21/06/2023 claimant from different hospitals, it would be just and proper to grant Rs.70,000/- towards Pain, Shock and Suffering.
Accordingly, the claimant would have also incurred expenses towards transportation and attendant charges as well as for the special diet.

The amount of Rs.15,000/- under the said heads has been granted by the learned Tribunal, is not in proportion to the evidence produced on record and hence, under the said heads,
it would be appropriate to grant a total sum of Rs.45,000/-.
Further, the actual loss of income has been granted for four months, while, the claimant could prove on record that he had taken the treatment for a long period.

Thus, considering his profession, as stated, he would not have been in a position to perform his profession for about six months and thus, the actual loss of income would be required to be granted accordingly.
Further, the Tribunal has granted the actual medical expenses of Rs.50,400/-.

In view of the above, the total compensation can be worked out as under:
 Head Amt. (Rs.)
Future loss of income 2,63,250/-
Pain, Shock and Suffering 70,000/-
 C/FA/308/2019 JUDGMENT DATED: 21/06/2023  Head Amt. (Rs.)
Special Diet, Attendant and Transportation 45,000/-
Charges Actual loss of income (for 6 months) 18,000/-
Medical expenses 50,400/-

Total 4,46,650/-
 Tribunal's award 3,29,200/-
 Difference 1,17,450/-
6.
For the forgoing discussion and observations, this appeal succeeds and is accordingly allowed in part.

The impugned judgment and award of the learned Tribunal is modified to the aforesaid extent and it is held that the appellant - claimant shall be entitled for a total sum of Rs.4,46,650/- towards compensation.

The Tribunal has awarded Rs.3,29,200/- and accordingly, differential amount of Rs.1,17,450/- shall be deposited within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of Kamruddin Rajabali Khoja vs Khimji Hathuji Jadeja on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150534708/

The appellant - claimant shall be entitled to 7.5% interest per annum on such enhanced amount of compensation.
6.1 The appellant - claimant is aged 70 years now.

Accordingly, considering the disability sustained by him, the Tribunal is directed C/FA/308/2019 JUDGMENT DATED: 21/06/2023 to disburse the total amount to the claimant together with interest accrued thereon on proper verification and following due procedure.
6.2 R&P, if received, be sent back forthwith.
